**Asymmetric Keys and Security Attacks**

**Objective:**

Students will be able to show they understand the creation and application of Asymmetric keys, as well as provide a summary regarding details about a recent security attack.

**Instructions:**

1. **Deliverable 1:** Detail the following sections of the diagram, each with a paragraph (3-5 sentences). The sections are Key Creation (top left), Ensuring Confidentiality (bottom left), and Ensuring Authenticity (right).

**The first section of the diagram shows the creation of a public and private key pair. The private key is kept secret while the public key is distributed to anyone that wants it. Only the private key can decrypt things encrypted with the public key and vice versa.**

**The bottom left section shows how confidentiality can be ensured using a key-pair.  Anybody can use the public key to encrypt a message and send it over an insecure channel without worrying. Only the person who holds the private key is able to decrypt and read the message. This ensures only the intended recipient can see the information.**

**The section on the right demonstrates how a public and private key pair can be used to ensure authenticity. The person who holds the private key can use it to encrypt a message and post it publicly. Anyone with the public key can decrypt the message and know with 100% certainty that the message came from the trusted source and that the message was not tampered with. If a bad actor tries to impersonate the person who has the private key by encrypting a message with a key of their own, the public key will not be able to decrypt it which will show that the message was not from a trusted source.**

2. Research a recent security attack, exploit, break-in, or hack that occurred within the last two years. Then, write a short summary of the attack and include the source of your information.

**Deliverable 1:** What people or organizations were involved?
**On May 20, 2025,  Kettering Health was hit by a ransomware attack from a group called Interlock. ([Kettering Health](https://ketteringhealth.org/cybersecurity-incident-faq/))**

**Deliverable 2:** How does the technology/vulnerability/malware work?
**The specific vulnerability and malware used to compromise Kettering Health was not published, however there is information online about the Interlock ransomware group and what they commonly use. They are an opportunistic and financially motivated ransomware group. They do double extortion attacks, first they exfiltrate and encrypt data. Then targets that don't pay the ransom get their data published on their leak site ([Arctic Wolf Threat Research, 2025](https://arcticwolf.com/resources/blog/threat-actor-profile-interlock-ransomware/)).**

**Deliverable 3:** What was impacted? What kind of data and/or how much money was taken?
**The incident made Kettering Health cancel appointments, shut down around 600 digital applications, and switch to pen and paper to record patient information ([Steve Alder, 2026](https://www.hipaajournal.com/kettering-health-ransomware-attack/)). Interlock also stole and published 941 GB of data which included information from 1,695,382 individuals ([Farah Amod, 2026](https://www.paubox.com/blog/kettering-health-ransomware-hit-1.7m-confirmed-year-after-interlock-breach)). 

**Deliverable 4:** What steps could be taken to prevent similar attacks in the future?
**To prevent similar attacks in the future, Kettering Health ensured "All necessary security protocols, including network segmentation, enhanced monitoring, and updated access controls, are in place"([Kettering Health](https://ketteringhealth.org/cybersecurity-incident-faq/)). They should also ensure all systems are fully updated with the latest software patches.**

**Deliverable 5:** How were the different areas of the CIA triad impacted?
**All three areas of the CIA triad were impacted in this case. Confidentiality was breached because the data was exfiltrated and published on Interlock's website. Integrity was breached because their systems and data were encrypted after the data was exfiltrated. Last and definitely not least, availability was breached because the encryption forced Kettering Health to take down their systems for an extended period of time.**
